member: Marcus - Vibration Control and Damping Specialist
message:
Elena, Priya, Tomas, the hidden mass stays tuned just below the bridge mode so a small weight controls a bus-scale deck. In plain words a child on a swing steadies a bus, then the numbers that decide are the Den Hartog optimum re-check (E54) with 500 kg, about seven body weights, tuned to 1.85 Hz at 0.0956 damping ratio, and the resonant response simulation (E47) falling from 1.75 m/s squared to 0.103 m/s squared, a factor 17 reduction.

Elena, Priya, Tomas, the Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, secondary sprung mass plus dampers tuned to bridge mode) sags a fist height then shakes a thumbnail without hitting stops, and dense-crowd shaking stays comfortable. In plain words steady sag plus shake is hand width and violent becomes gentle braking, then the numbers that decide are the static sag calculation (E55) of 72.3 mm plus the dense-crowd stroke scaling (E53) of 20.1 mm giving the total compression calculation (E56) of 92.4 mm against plus-minus 50 mm dynamic stops in the bolted frame sketch (E37), and the TMD-controlled acceleration scaling (E52) of 0.545 m/s squared, 0.0556 times gravity like gentle bus braking and plausible, below the 1.00 m/s squared bound in the Experimental and Numerical Study on Dynamics of Two Footbridges with Different Shapes of Girders (E38).

Ready, because tuning, clearance with stop margin, and comfort close jointly on buildable hardware.
